**Solution 1 (278): REJECT.** Its formula $S(j,k)=4+2(2k-j)$ undercounts. Take $(j,k)=(11,10)$: one unshaded rectangle must touch all 10 shaded ones, so the contact graph is a star. If the center has $L$ leaves, each leaf's two ends either sit at a corner of the center or create a reflex vertex of the polygon. Counting ends gives at least $2L-4$ reflex vertices, so the polygon has at least $4L-4$ sides. For $L=10$ that is 36, not the 22 the solution uses. The same counting shows $S(5,4)=12$ (the plus sign), not 10.

**Solution 2 (130): REJECT.** Its claim that a rectangle can carry $\lceil 2j/3\rceil$ independent rectangles is false. Shaded rectangles inside a rectangle split it into components, and two unshaded rectangles can create at most $u+1$ components, so $k\le\lceil j/2\rceil$. For $j=15$ the solution's value $M(15)=10$ exceeds the true maximum of 8. It also assigns $S=4$ to $(11,10)$, which is impossible by the star argument above.

**Solution 3 (272): REJECT.** Its table has $S(11,10)=28$, but the star argument forces at least 36. Its comb model also has the wrong side counts: a comb with $t$ teeth on a base has $4t$ sides, not the $6$, $8$, $10$ it lists. Its total therefore cannot be trusted.

I did not complete a fully rigorous lower bound for every $(j,k)$ in the range, so I have not verified the exact total. A candidate formula $S(j,k)=4\max(1,2k-j)$ fits every check I made, but I have not confirmed it, so I am not stating a final value.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
